description: This is the symbolic head of the republic, an honorary title given to the leader of the merchants' guild. They have no real power within the guild or the civilization, but are often called upon for advice and guidance. They expect almost royal treatment, as befits their status as the figurehead of the republic.

The merchant master councillor is one of two guildmasters who act as the chief decision-makers of both the republic and the merchants' guild. They oversee guild operations, decide on trade policy and warfare. While running their own businesses as merchants, they mandate trade operations. Due to their aristocratic status, they demand lavish living quarters.

The merchant master magistrate holds the highest office of justice in the republic, charged with upholding the law and ensuring the safety and protection of the people. While running their own businesses as merchants, they mandate trade operations. Due to their aristocratic status, they demand lavish living quarters.

The merchant master ambassador holds the highest diplomatic office within the merchants' guild and is responsible for receiving and hosting diplomatic guests. While running their own businesses as merchants, they mandate trade operations. Due to their aristocratic status, they demand lavish living quarters.

The merchant master steward holds the highest administrative office of the republic, entrusted with the careful management of its resources. They oversee tax collection, secure the food supply, direct construction, and manage the guilds' housekeeping. While running their own businesses as merchants, they mandate trade operations. Due to their aristocratic status, they demand lavish living quarters.

The merchant guild apprentice serves the guild by delivering messages and attending to the needs of its masters. Through diligent service and reliability, they support the daily workings of the guild while striving to prove their worth and rise through its ranks.
The Captain-general is the highest-ranking officer of the republican military, commanding their subordinate captains. Due to their high status, they demand lavish living quarters.

The captain is an officer in the republican military, responsible for leading a squad of 8 soldiers and are entrusted with escorting tax collectors and patrolling the borders. Due to their position, they require comfortable living quarters befitting their status.
Free merchants are the 'pillars of society'. The republic rests on the principles of freedom and commerce. Approximately 2% of the population belongs to this group.

The trade agent is an administrator assigned to the fortress by the Merchants' Guild. Their appointment designates the site as a chartered trade post. They appoint clerks to assist them with their tasks. They are empowered to issue trade mandates, defining which goods may be produced or exchanged. A modest office is required.

The trade administrator is an official appointed by the Merchants' Guild. Their presence elevates the fortress to a chartered market town. They appoint clerks to assist them with their tasks. They are empowered to issue expanded trade and production mandates. Office improvements are required.

The trade director is a senior official appointed by the Merchants' Guild. Their presence elevates the fortress to a chartered merchant city. They appoint clerks to assist them with their tasks. They are empowered to issue expanded trade and production mandates. A modest office is required.

The chief commissioner is a principal official appointed by the Merchants' Guild. Their presence elevates the fortress to a principal mercantile city. They appoint clerks to assist with administrative tasks and, when required, can dispatch military forces to protect the republic's interests. Their mandates broadly determine permitted production and commerce. Decent living quarters are required.

The grand commissioner is the highest official appointed by the Merchants' Guild. Their presence elevates the site to the supreme 'citadel of commerce'. They appoint clerks to assist them with their tasks. They hold the authority to issue supreme mandates governing commerce, production, and sanctioned military expeditions. Decent living quarters are required. (1/6)

The merchant guilds journeyman serves as a trusted representative of the guild in diplomatic affairs and is responsible for overseeing the trade routes between settlements. While conducting business as a merchant, they mandate the flow of goods and communication across the republic. Their position entails clear but modest and practical living requirements.

At the grand summit of the republic's burgher society, they form the proud crest of the metropolis. Their names travel along trade-roads, spoken with respect in distant markets. Their halls are the finest a free people grant, symbols of renown gained not by duty, but by the standing the republic bestows.

Grand in mandate, they stand at the summit of what a free city can bestow. Their names carry beyond mountain roads and river borders, spoken with regard in distant halls. Their quarters - finest a free people can grant - reflect the renown of those who shape not only the city, but its place in the world.

Honored among their peers, they tighten the weave of civic function. At their behest a clerk of stores is appointed, ensuring that supplies and lifeblood flow with order rather than chance. Their dwellings, too, grow richer in finish and provision, echoing the authority they quietly accumulate.

Highly honored within the walls, they stand among the most secure beneficiaries of the city's newly recognized freedom. Though their responsibilities scarcely exceed those of any other citizen, their name commands courtesy, and their dwellings - rich in craft and quiet indulgence - signal a status that needs no proclamation.

Esteemed and firmly rooted in duty, their households rise with them. Even their spouses are released from the humble labors of the common day, and their quarters expand in comfort and refinement - an acknowledgment that their stature now stands far beyond the tools of survival.

Here they reach the upper ease of republican life, their role largely ceremonial, their obligations light as hammered silver. Their households mirror this privilege, adorned with luxuries that once belonged only to governors and clerks. They carry themselves as esteemed figures who know the charter did more than enriching the city - it elevated them.

Distinguished by responsibility, they extend their concern to the safety of all. Under their authority, a civic guard is named - steel drawn not for conquest, but for the well-being of the city that depends on them.

Marked by steady rise rather than burden, they move through the republic with the quiet assurance of those who no longer answer to the harsher demands of governance. Their comforts deepen - well-lit halls, ample storage, and furnishings chosen for pleasure rather than necessity - small honors they now accept as ordinary.

Notable in standing, their hands turn from toil to governance. Freed from menial burdens, they begin to entrust tasks to clerks so that their attention may rest wholly on guiding the young settlement's path.

At this standing they have become figures of notable prosperity within the chartered city, beholden to few tasks beyond maintaining its good repute. Their living spaces expand with polished stone, crafted timber and shiny artifacts, not so subtle signs that they now dwell on the easier side of the republic's labor.

Recognized now not only for labor but for judgment, they shoulder the quiet weight of order. From among them emerges the first keeper of justice - the bailiff - appointed so that fairness may take root before law is written.

Further settled into the life of a free republic, they shoulder little beyond the obligations of decency, their responsibilities far gentler than in their citizen days. Their quarters grow correspondingly refined, and they make no secret of expecting such comforts now that the Merchants' Guild has placed its seal upon the city.

With the settlement taking form, they refine their quarters, allowing themselves a measure of comfort befitting those who endure the brunt of early hardship. A small elevation, yet a sign that the city begins to breathe.

They are recognized as aristocrats of the capital, wealthy by position rather than office. Their lives unfold in cultivated comfort, shaped by the city's centrality and its steady abundance. They expect deference as a matter of course, though still observe the outward forms of civic restraint.

As aristocrats they grow openly rich, their households expanding in scale and refinement. Prosperity gathers around them with little explanation, and they begin to compare their standing not to citizens, but to lesser courts. Requests for exceptional lodging are made softly, framed as convenience.

Here they are, living in lavish surroundings that rival princely estates. Their presence reshapes protocol, and accommodations once reserved for visiting rulers are no longer unthinkable. Such expectations raise brows, yet are often granted to avoid offense.

At this height, living in open splendor, their estates mirroring royal courts in scale and ceremony. They measure themselves against kings without irony, and treat monarchic honors as fitting recognition. Objections persist, but tradition bends under their abundance.

They stand like monarchs in all but crown, extravagantly secure and unchallenged. Royal quarters are assumed, their lifestyle indistinguishable from sovereign rule. The capital may deny them kingship, yet indulges them as though it had already conceded it.
The doctor is responsible for the health and well-being of the settlement's inhabitants. They require adequate facilities and resources to perform their duties effectively.

The captain of the republican guard is an officer in the republican military, responsible for leading a squad of 8 soldiers and are considered the only professional soldiers of the republic. Due to their esteemed position, they require comfortable living quarters befitting their status. - The republican guard consist of 24 guards, divided into three squads of 8 soldiers each. Only the capital is allowed to deploy a republican guard.

The captain of the municipal guard is an officer in the republican military, responsible for leading a squad of 8 soldiers and is entrusted with escorting tax collectors and patrolling the borders. Due to their esteemed position, they require comfortable living quarters befitting their status. - The municipal guard consist of 8 guards. Only the mercantile cities are allowed to deploy a municipal guard.

The captain of the civic guard is an officer in the republican military, responsible for leading a squad of 8 soldiers and are entrusted the protection of the interests of the citizens. Due to their esteemed position, they require comfortable living quarters befitting their status. - The civic guard consist of 8 guards. Only the settlements with a minimum population of 170 are allowed to deploy a civic guard.

The Marshal is the second highest-ranking officer of the republican military. Although not directly responsible for command, they are indispensable in preparing missions. Due to their high status, they demand lavish living quarters.

The executioner (hammer) is responsible for carrying out capital punishments within the settlement. They require specialized skills in using the chosen method of execution. Any of the executioner types may be appointed by the player, giving the option to select the preferred method of execution. - Executioners are appointable when the settlement becomes the capital of the republic.

The inquisitor is responsible for investigating and rooting out heresy and dissent within the settlement. Inquisitors are only assigned for conquered settlements.

The bailiff is the chief law enforcement officer of the settlement, responsible for maintaining order and overseeing the constables. Due to their high status, they demand comfortable living quarters. The bailiff commands two constables who assist in law enforcement duties throughout the settlement.
